Neither one gives you an edge — Australian and Irish passports are treated identically for Vietnam entry. Vietnam does not have a visa-free exemption for either nationality, so no matter which passport you travel on, you'll need to get a visa in advance.

For both, the recommended pathway is the e-Visa:
- Stay: up to 90 days
- Cost: USD 25 (single entry) or USD 50 (multiple entry)
- Processing: 2–3 business days (faster/expedited options exist at extra cost)
- Apply at the official portal: https://evisa.gov.vn/
- Entry allowed by air, land, or sea at any approved e-Visa port (83 ports tracked in this dataset)

A couple of practical notes that apply either way: your passport needs at least 180 days of validity remaining from your entry date, and since the e-Visa is open to all nationalities, you could technically apply under either passport — just make sure the passport you register for the e-Visa is the one you actually travel and enter with, since they need to match.

Bottom line: pick whichever passport is more convenient for you to travel on (e.g., better onward visa-free access elsewhere, or the one that's currently valid with more validity buffer) — it won't change your Vietnam entry requirements, since both Australians and Irish citizens go through the same e-Visa process.

This is based on data as of 2026-08-17 from the bundled policy dataset — I'd recommend double-checking current requirements at evisa.gov.vn before you book, since visa policies can change.
